newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICAN INTERNATIONAL TINKLER JOINS BARNSLEY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICAN INTERNATIONAL TINKLER JOINS BARNSLEY.

text.p: South African international midfielder Eric Tinkler joined newly-promoted English premier league side Barnsley on Tuesday -- then admitted he had never heard of them a year ago.
Tinkler, 26, signed a three-year contract following a 650,000 pounds ($1.1 million) move from Italian side Cagliari.

But for political red tape he could have been playing in England for 10 years. He joined Coventry City on trial as a 16-year-old and despite several appearances in the reserves during his six months there, was ultimately refused a work permit and he moved to Portugal before joining Cagliari last season.
Tinkler, a long-time Chelsea fan, admits he has finally realised a long-held ambition. He said: "I am very happy to be at Barnsley.
"It has been my lifetime's dream to play in English football ever since I grew up as a Chelsea supporter.
"English football is followed more than any other in South Africa, more than Spanish or Italian football. I'm sure there will be a few following Barnsley now.
"But it's been a long road to get here. The politics of my country a decade ago never allowed me to make my dream come true in playing for Coventry.
"I played in the reserves against the likes of Manchester City, Sheffield United and Newcastle United and came up against many quality players. But I never managed to play against the elite.
"But I must admit I didn't even know who Barnsley were this time last year, so I never thought I would end up signing for them."
Tinkler is Barnsley's third foreign signing this summer following Macedonian international Georgi Hristov and German goalkeeper Lars Leese from Bayer Leverkusen.
They are due to complete their fourth signing on Wednesdsay when Slovenian international defender Ales Krizan joins.
